title: Trump Makes a Deal to Buy Russian Diesel to Lower Fuel Prices
summary:
President Donald Trump has announced a deal to bring Russian diesel fuel into the United States. He says the plan should help bring down high fuel prices, but Ukraine's president strongly disagrees with it.

Diesel is a fuel used by trucks, trains, farm machines and many other vehicles. In recent months, the price of gasoline and especially diesel has jumped in America. The BBC reports that this is linked to a war involving Iran that began in February and has affected energy prices around the world. Higher fuel prices have also made many other things cost more.

On Friday, Trump said Russian President Vladimir Putin had agreed to release 300,000 tonnes of diesel right away, then 500,000 tonnes in November and another million tonnes after that. Trump said more could follow later. The US Treasury issued a temporary license allowing Russian diesel into the market and is pausing some sanctions, which are penalties on trade, until April 7.

Putin said Russia was willing to supply oil products to the US and other countries, but he did not give amounts.

Some experts doubt the plan will help much. One investment expert, Tim Armitage, said the first delivery was "relatively small" compared with how much diesel Americans use each day, so it would not make a big difference at the gas pump. He called it a "slightly desperate move" before next month's midterm elections.

Ukraine has been fighting against Russia's invasion. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky called the deal a gift to Putin and said such gifts "will not work for peace." The United Kingdom said it would keep up its pressure on Russia and keep supporting Ukraine.
why_it_matters: Fuel prices affect the cost of food, travel and goods for American families, and the deal also tests how countries balance their own needs against pressure on Russia over its war in Ukraine.

background_read: Diesel is a fuel made from crude oil, and it powers most trucks, trains and farm machines, so its price affects the cost of moving and growing almost everything.
When fuel becomes scarce or costly anywhere, prices tend to rise worldwide because oil and fuel are traded globally.
Russia invaded Ukraine, and many countries, including the US and UK, placed sanctions on Russia to limit the money it earns from selling energy.
Buying Russian diesel means easing some of those sanctions, which is why Ukraine and its supporters object.
